Question:
The operation \(\otimes\) is defined for all nonzero numbers by \[a\otimes b =\dfrac{a^{2}}{b}.\]

Determine \[[(1\otimes 2)\otimes 3]-[1\otimes (2\otimes 3)].\]
Solution:
The rule \(a\otimes b=a^2/b\) means to square the first operand and divide by the second. The parentheses determine which operation to do first.

For the first bracket,
\[
1\otimes2=\frac12,
\qquad
(1\otimes2)\otimes3
=\frac{(1/2)^2}{3}
=\frac1{12}.
\]
For the second bracket,
\[
2\otimes3=\frac43,
\qquad
1\otimes(2\otimes3)
=\frac{1^2}{4/3}
=\frac34.
\]
The original operands and the intermediate values \(\frac12\) and \(\frac43\) are all nonzero, so these operations are defined. Subtracting gives
\[
\frac1{12}-\frac34
=\frac1{12}-\frac9{12}
=-\frac8{12}
=\boxed{-\frac23},
\]
choice A.
